Class Infrared

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.io.ir.Infrared
public final class Infrared extends Object
Serial bytes over modulated infrared light, recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno and bit-banged on two plain pins, with no Arduino library. It is the transport under protocols such as RcxRemote.

Wiring: an IR receiver module with a 38 kHz demodulator (e.g. TSOP38238 or VS1838B), whose output idles high and goes low during a burst, on the receive pin; an IR LED with a series resistor on the transmit pin, driven with a software 38 kHz carrier. A burst is a 0 bit, so the levels match a UART's. Either pin may be -1 to use only the other direction.

Each byte is framed as a start bit, eight data bits least significant first, an odd parity bit and a stop bit. Both directions are blocking and busy-wait on the bit timing, so call them from the main loop, not while Delay.millis is waiting. Works on both boards.

    • echoByte

      public static int echoByte(int value, int latencyMicros)
      Transmits one framed byte like writeByte(int) while reading it back through the receiver module, which hears the board's own IR LED. Each bit is sampled in the middle of its time plus latencyMicros, to allow for the demodulator's response delay (typically 100 to 400 microseconds). Returns the byte received, 0..255, TIMEOUT if nothing was heard or a pin is unset, or FRAMING_ERROR. Used to test the wiring and the carrier timing: a working pair returns the byte sent for some latency.

    • mark

      public static void mark(int micros)
      Transmits a burst of the 38 kHz carrier for micros microseconds. With space(int), it builds protocols that encode bits in pulse lengths rather than as serial bytes, such as PowerFunctionsRemote; the transmit pin must be set by begin(int, int, int) (the baud rate is ignored by these two calls).

    • space

      public static void space(int micros)
      Keeps the IR LED dark for micros microseconds.
